title: Plural of long-vowel words
summary: For these long-vowel words, shorten the double vowel and add -ita/-itä: maa (“country”) → maita.
objectives: Form the plural partitive in this bounded word family.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: A case is a word form used for a grammatical job. The dictionary form is the form used to look up a word. The partitive has several uses; it does not always mean “some”. Here you practise forming the word, so no sentence construction is required.

In these one-syllable words, shorten the final double vowel to one vowel, then add -ita/-itä. Plural i comes before the partitive -ta/-tä. Choose a/ä using the original word’s vowel harmony; neutral-only tee takes -itä. Singular forms keep the long vowel, while these plural forms shorten it.
keyPoints: Learn each word with its pattern; a similar final letter does not guarantee the same stem.

steps: Shorten aa to a and add -ita: maa → maita.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “country”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.
Shorten uu to u and add -ita: puu → puita.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “tree”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.
Shorten ee to e and add -itä: tee → teitä.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “tea”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.
Shorten uu to u and add -ita: suu → suita.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “mouth”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.
Shorten uu to u and add -ita: kuu → kuita.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “moon”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.
Shorten ää to ä and add -itä: pää → päitä.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “head”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.
Shorten ää to ä and add -itä: jää → jäitä.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “ice”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.
Shorten ää to ä and add -itä: sää → säitä.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “weather”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.

commonMistakes: Do not keep both original vowels before plural i.
Do not copy the singular -ta/-tä form.
Different dictionary words can share a plural form; use the base word shown.
